result.keyword: What's the best project management tool for a startup?
result.markdown:
For most startups, **Linear is the best project management tool if you're building a tech or SaaS company.** If you're running a broader business with marketing, sales, operations, and product teams, I'd lean toward **ClickUp or Asana**\.

The best choice depends on three things\:

1. How big your team is.
2. Whether you're building software or running a general business.
3. Whether you want something lightweight or a complete operating system for your company.

My biggest recommendation: **Don't overcomplicate project management early on.** A startup needs visibility, accountability, clear priorities, and fast execution—not a complicated system that takes hours to maintain.

## My top 5 project management tools for startups

![Projects – Linear Docs](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/a0Bz1u1BDTqROjGm9ELZZ6WZ6dLGVnX6_hsL_Cg0fc0tRbCe9nfMGH3JPnpT-OgzlFKdMd3tFMKpmxGnYWzQDNxDyAto92CxFYJ3s6aAwDzQfzgkmx7jeqs49Ap71zaAgOVuWYjKdS8EYJZkTYKc-fYdBT7b-8HVIlp-mKGEyy6LAouz74wxYMP5Nmubb7Wg?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Linear**

(Best for tech startups)

- Excellent product roadmaps and sprint planning.
- Great for engineering and product teams.
- Clean, fast interface with minimal clutter.
- Less suited to managing every business function.

My pick for SaaS and software companies.

[Linear website](https://linear.app/)

---

![SaaS Website Design: 15 Examples to Inspire Your Redesign](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/uaiISLb5gef6BNwGlb3rsTNQNLtZ5tcXKUykRGIm8vBtxyp1mf1gKMsSGHU2L5fy-H4FOU5xMxu86StGz0GpW2dIQi5vS0yuHXu3Z-0eQVEc-1c929-_kNVZw4ne7Vhd84PF-0aUq2sE9FuCoNdV-9O9TOGsDRMyJYs1OQjrW7mZLUosVDLfqA95_O6udjGW?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. ClickUp**

(Best all-in-one)

- Tasks, docs, goals, dashboards and automations.
- Useful for marketing, operations, sales and product.
- Highly customizable.
- Can become overwhelming if overconfigured.

My pick if you want one central workspace.

[ClickUp website](https://clickup.com/)

---

![El espacio de trabajo con IA que trabaja para ti. | Notion](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/R_yUfovyKFmaJQEcfVv4jYuyXeaWYkav6gYzicaCMWWqPfPzNaErfGMOWNqjMzISqpbXUMnimSX3Mgt80_s-U0wTwwCsZLCjRzqMBHclvcNBTvqjF9hox5eli0U18V-Fagushdua4nuePC1nB-tAV6pX9UJfQFTWzmLOiW_jRcRBcUU--t9jq3Blb9nNSH9c?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Notion**

- Excellent company wiki and documentation.
- Project trackers, meeting notes and databases.
- Great for early-stage teams.
- Less powerful for complex project execution.

My pick for a small founding team.

[Notion website](https://www.notion.com/)

---

![Asana Project Management Software. Teams don’t lose track of work with Asana. • Asana | Asana | 21 comments](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/RvIYplIFupIXp1KqtkuDy3jxnmylal5BHnUQ3fTTxbOC51qz1Qem0EzUbde4cZ3lLTT5HAh7AVURPn69eZTKw1fHYMw2GSvQyG7DJZXLNS30WfYJcXCMlk9cWylRYXmiW10i0EJU7jPeRTQqL5PEuHI8xeF3_0oRLHsx4lSVCE_zhH-Kh6OSnZQ77xreCMig?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Asana**

- Excellent task ownership and accountability.
- Good project timelines and dependencies.
- Easy for nontechnical employees to adopt.
- Less flexible as an all-in-one workspace.

My pick for cross-functional teams.

[Asana website](https://asana.com/)

---

![Ações de empresas sediadas em Israel caem depois de ataque do Hamas | Investimento no Exterior | Valor Investe](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/36x_cwrhZexLcQp_PPhIYwxdo-eIjJhxRtXGGuXtiItvsKAspi9ayyltwcS8oIymzML9f7HDc-P4aKAPI2Q3BRZUeaBaKvjUh8Pt_WO8gkzwbfZ2j3rjih0KDtdAWvkwjQf57Ho0V8qI8KVSwtNUkiA_TkuDnsDh3lBdCvh38KVCkOqz6gvN1OP5U5ObfjGX?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. Monday.com**

- Visual project dashboards.
- Strong marketing and operations workflows.
- Useful reporting and automation.
- Can get expensive as the team grows.

My pick for visually managing business operations.

[Monday.com website](https://monday.com/)

## What I'd actually implement at a startup

I'd start with a simple structure\:

| Area | What to manage |
|--------|--------|
| Company goals | Quarterly objectives and KPIs |
| Product | Roadmap and feature priorities |
| Marketing | Campaigns and content calendar |
| Sales | Leads, deals and follow-ups |
| Operations | Internal projects and processes |
| Weekly execution | Owners, deadlines and blockers |


Keep one rule: every task needs an owner, a deadline, and a clear definition of done.
